Onboarding
You were asked to arrive with an agent working (
setup guide

). If you did,
help the others in your group. If yours will not run, say so at the start rather than at the
end. You will pair up and do the typing yourself. Save or email yourself whatever comes out
before you leave, since it will be on somebody else’s laptop and you will need it on Friday.
Prompting

Groups of three, or two. Each student picks a different phenomenon, so between you the group
covers all three. All three came from what this class submitted on Exercise 0.

A graduating senior sends nearly the same résumé to a long list of postings. A few employers
reply with an invitation to a first-round interview, most send a rejection, and some never
answer. People count different things when they describe how it went: replies, interviews, or
offers. Callback rates vary by field and by year, and two people applying to the same jobs can
see very different results. University career offices publish callback and placement rates from
their own surveys, and some job platforms collect application outcomes too. Advice about how
many applications to send circulates as round numbers, and some applicants report sending
several hundred without a single interview.

A stock index finishes each trading day above, below, or level with its previous close. Across
long stretches of U.S. market history, up days have been somewhat more common than down days.
Newsletter writers, fund managers and anonymous accounts publish calls on the market’s
direction, over horizons that run from the next close to the next year. Some of them have long
runs of correct calls behind them, and those runs are what the marketing quotes. Daily closing
prices for the major indexes are free and go back decades, so a call written down in advance
can be checked later against what happened.

A supply contract states limits for a part, and it may also require that at least 99% of parts
fall inside them. Lines drift as tools wear and materials change. Inspecting every part is
often impractical, so a company checks a sample from each batch and decides on that basis
whether to accept the batch, hold it, or send it back. Both errors are expensive: rejecting a
good batch holds up production, and accepting a bad one ships defects to a customer. A line
that is meeting its target will still
produce the occasional sample that looks bad, and a line that has started to drift will still
produce samples that look fine. How many parts get inspected, and what result triggers a
rejection, are set by the contract, by industry standards, and by what the defects would cost.

Frame it as a modelling problem to your agent, in a prompt of your own. You can leave it open
and see what the agent does with it. You can also try constraining it, by making explicit
assumptions or by focusing on the particular aspects of the phenomenon that interest you.
Either is a reasonable thing to do.
Whatever else you ask for, ask for these:
an explanation of its approach, and a justification for it;
its assumptions, made explicit rather than left in the code;
artifacts: markdown documents, runnable code, etc.
Investigating

Look at what the agent actually produced, and run the code if there is code. Open the files
rather than taking its word for what is in them. Some agents write into the folder you opened
and some write somewhere else and tell you the path, so read to the end of the answer before
you conclude it made nothing. Keep the conversation open, since you will need it on Friday.
Interpreting

About a minute each. Explain your model and its assumptions to the others in your group,
without code and without formulas.

Then take note of any similarities in the models of the three phenomena. Are there common
structures or assumptions? Or do they differ, and if so, how?
Get this far before we stop for the quiz.
Interrogating — after section

The questions on Ed ask what your model assumed without being told to, what mathematics it
uses, where any of its numbers came from, and how you would ‘validate’ it. AM215 students have
one more, on how you would ‘verify’ the code. Then a few general questions about how the
session went, and a last short set looking ahead to next week.

The boxes are short and there is one per thing asked. Due Friday at 11:59 pm, and none of it
needs a working agent.

Submissions are de-identified before analysis and stored separately from grades. We do not
collect your agent conversations, only what the form asks for. Full statement: the syllabus,
under Use of AI tools → Data use in this course.
